city_personality.one_line_summary: Beijing is strongest when imperial scale, hutong daily life, and modern city contrast are arranged as layered routes rather than stacked as a generic landmark checklist.
explore_strengths: night atmosphere in selected urban zones
signature_contrasts: imperial order vs everyday hutong life
old capital texture vs contemporary creative energy
formal landmarks vs relaxed neighborhood wandering
avoid_generic_framing: Do not reduce Beijing to a famous landmark checklist.
Do not describe every route as grand, cultural, and profound without district texture.
Do not make all traveler types start from the same landmark pair and end with the same food rhythm.
Do not use empty big-city praise that could fit any capital city.

district_knowledge.name: Imperial Core
mobility_notes: Best used as one major anchor instead of chaining multiple heavy heritage stops.
Family routes should keep the day geographically tight after this district.
Works well when softened by hutong or food texture later in the day.

district_knowledge.name: Hutong and Shichahai
mobility_notes: Excellent for walking-heavy half days with low transfer friction.
Best when paired with one earlier landmark cluster instead of another distant district-heavy route.
Evening value is much stronger than a rushed midday pass-through.

district_knowledge.name: 798 Art District
mobility_notes: Works best as a focused modern-culture half day rather than a quick insert into an old-city route.
Not ideal for low-friction family itineraries centered on classic landmarks.
Pair with another eastern urban district instead of imperial-core overloading.

district_knowledge.name: Sanlitun and Modern Urban Core
district_knowledge.role: modern lifestyle, nightlife, and youth-energy anchor
mobility_notes: Most useful as an evening closer or modern-contrast half day.
Can feel generic if used without a clear urban-lifestyle angle.
Should not replace city-specific texture for every traveler type.

poi_knowledge.name: Forbidden City Outer Axis Visit
risks: Very high repeat risk across many Beijing plans.
Can dominate the day and flatten variety if always used as the default anchor.
Crowd and walking load can make family pacing feel heavy when paired poorly.
poi_knowledge.description: Use as a strong history anchor only when the route truly needs imperial scale.

poi_knowledge.name: Jingshan Viewpoint
risks: Can become formulaic if always paired mechanically with the same imperial-core route.
Adds value only when the route benefits from contrast and viewpoint payoff.
poi_knowledge.description: Useful when a heavy heritage route needs a scenic and photogenic release point.

poi_knowledge.name: Shichahai Hutong Walk
risks: Can feel too similar to other hutong content if no route angle is defined.
Needs pacing and nearby food logic to avoid turning into generic wandering.
poi_knowledge.description: A strong source of lived-in Beijing texture and a reliable route softener after major landmarks.

poi_knowledge.name: Nanluoguxiang and Side Lanes
risks: Very easy to overuse as a default youth-oriented Beijing stop.
Main-lane focus can feel generic unless side-lane texture is emphasized.
poi_knowledge.description: Best used when the plan wants approachable food, light wandering, and a younger neighborhood feel.

poi_knowledge.name: 798 Core Gallery Walk
risks: Weak fit for plans that need classic Beijing identity only.
Can feel detached if paired with distant heritage areas in a dense one-day route.
poi_knowledge.description: Useful when the route needs a clear old-vs-new contrast rather than a pure heritage shape.

poi_knowledge.name: Sanlitun Urban Evening Walk
risks: Can read as generic upscale urban content if not tied to a clear traveler angle.
Not strong enough to carry a Beijing plan alone without city-specific contrast.
poi_knowledge.description: Best for routes that want modern-night Beijing energy after a more character-heavy daytime path.

food_knowledge.name: Qianmen Traditional Food Zone
food_knowledge.note: Useful when the route needs traditional Beijing food identity near a landmark-heavy day.

food_knowledge.name: Shichahai Hutong Food Area
food_knowledge.note: Best when the route wants local texture, moderate spend, and a natural connection between walking and eating.

food_knowledge.name: Nanluoguxiang Snack Lanes
food_knowledge.category: youthful snack and casual food area
food_knowledge.note: Most useful for student and solo routes that want flexible, low-commitment food rhythm.

food_knowledge.name: Sanlitun Modern Dining Zone
food_knowledge.note: Best when the route wants contemporary urban mood rather than traditional Beijing food identity.

preferred_route_patterns: one major heritage anchor plus one nearby softer walking district
landmark morning plus relaxed food-and-stroll afternoon
avoid_patterns: imperial core plus 798 plus Sanlitun in one day
too many long transfers after a heavy landmark start
pace_notes: Balanced pace is usually stronger than dense pacing.
Each day should feel geographically clear and easy to recover from.
value_notes: A strong family Beijing route should feel iconic but not exhausting.

preferred_route_patterns: scenic viewpoint plus hutong walk plus evening dining
old-city texture day followed by modern-night contrast
creative district afternoon plus stylish urban dinner
avoid_patterns: all-function landmark stacks with no atmosphere shift
museum-like pacing across the whole day
pace_notes: Afternoon-to-evening sequencing often works better than early hard-start density.
value_notes: A strong couple route should soften Beijing's scale with mood, texture, and memorable evening scenes.

preferred_route_patterns: creative district afternoon plus lively evening area
one iconic stop balanced by lighter neighborhood movement
avoid_patterns: too much formal heritage in one day with weak local playfulness
pace_notes: Balanced to slightly dense can work if the route remains district-clustered.
value_notes: A strong student route should feel fun, affordable, and visibly different from a standard sightseeing plan.

preferred_route_patterns: landmark-light day with strong citywalk texture
heritage anchor followed by independent wandering district
creative district plus neighborhood food route
pace_notes: Solo routes should leave room for flexible wandering and unhurried observation.
value_notes: A strong solo Beijing route should feel self-directed, layered, and rich in city texture.

half_day_combinations.name: Imperial Core Heritage Half Day
half_day_combinations.note: Best when the route needs a clear Beijing history anchor without overloading later movement.

half_day_combinations.name: Hutong and Shichahai Soft Walk Half Day
half_day_combinations.note: Best for low-friction texture, food rhythm, and atmosphere.

half_day_combinations.name: 798 Contemporary Contrast Half Day
half_day_combinations.note: Useful when the route needs modern creative Beijing rather than another old-city loop.

half_day_combinations.name: Sanlitun Modern Evening Half Day
half_day_combinations.note: Best as an evening finisher rather than the full identity of the day.

one_day_routes.name: Classic Beijing With Soft Neighborhood Finish
one_day_routes.logic: Use a strong heritage anchor in the first half, then shift into walkable hutong and food texture to avoid a rigid landmark-only day.

one_day_routes.name: Creative East-Side Contrast Day
one_day_routes.logic: Use 798 for contemporary visual culture, then close with modern urban dining or nightlife energy.

one_day_routes.name: Student-Friendly Low-Pressure Citywalk Day
one_day_routes.logic: Keep the route snack-friendly, walkable, and flexible instead of landmark-heavy.

avoid_combinations.reason: Too transfer-heavy for a clean one-day route and weakens the city texture arc.
Stacking too many heavy heritage anchors creates repetition and reduces traveler-type differences.
Modern urban nightlife alone is not enough to represent Beijing's distinctive Explore identity.

editor_notes: This file is a V2 test dataset only.
It is intentionally selective rather than exhaustive.
The focus is traveler differentiation and route-shaping value.
